artworks.title: Portrait statue of Mausolus
artworks.description: Colossal marble from the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus (British Museum): the satrap-king whose tomb gave every later mausoleum its name. Hellenistic drapery and beard fix Mausolus as the mortal for whom Artemisia raised the Wonder of the World.

artworks.title: The Mausoleum at Halicarnassus
artworks.description: Knab’s reconstruction paints the stepped pyramid, chariot, and colonnade Pliny described — the tomb of Mausolus as nineteenth-century imagination still saw the Wonder. The king’s afterlife is architecture: his name outlived his city as a common noun for grand burial.

popCulture.title: Mausoleum at Halicarnassus
popCulture.description: One of the Seven Wonders — built for Mausolus of Caria by Artemisia — the monument that made his name a synonym for any splendid tomb.

popCulture.title: mausoleum
popCulture.description: English and the Romance languages keep Mausolus inside the word for a monumental tomb — linguistic reception rarer and more durable than any portrait.
